drills.q: What is a warp, and why does divergent branching within one cost real cycles?
drills.a: A fixed group of 32 threads executing the same instruction in lockstep on an SM. Divergent threads cause the hardware to serialize both branch paths, masking off inactive threads for each pass -- a 2-way divergence costs roughly double the cycles of no divergence.

drills.q: What is occupancy, and why does it matter more on a GPU than a similarly-named CPU metric?
drills.a: The ratio of resident warps to an SM's max (64/SM on H100). A stalled warp lets the scheduler switch to another resident warp at ~0 cost since full register state lives permanently in the register file, unlike a CPU thread switch requiring save/restore. Low occupancy leaves the SM idle waiting on memory instead of hiding that latency.

drills.q: Why does nvidia-smi showing 100% GPU utilization not mean the GPU is being used efficiently?
drills.a: It reports whether any kernel is running, not how efficiently it uses compute. A memory-bandwidth-bound kernel (e.g. batch=1 LLM inference) can show 100% utilization while compute units sit substantially idle waiting on HBM -- check achieved occupancy/bandwidth utilization via a real profiler instead.

drills.q: Why is LLM inference at batch size 1 memory-bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound?
drills.a: Generating one token requires loading the entire model's weights from HBM but performs relatively few FLOPs per token relative to that data volume -- low arithmetic intensity. Compute units are capable of far higher throughput than bandwidth can feed them at this ratio, leaving them mostly idle.

drills.q: Explain continuous batching and why it beats static/request-level batching.
drills.a: Static batching waits for every request in a fixed group to finish, wasting slots on requests that finish early. Continuous batching removes finished requests and adds new ones at every decode step, keeping the batch continuously full. vLLM reports up to ~23x throughput with reduced p50 latency; Orca reported up to ~36.9x vs static batching.

drills.q: What does PagedAttention add on top of continuous batching, and what problem does it solve?
drills.a: Continuous batching solves scheduling; PagedAttention solves memory layout -- it manages the KV cache in fixed-size, non-contiguous pages instead of one large contiguous block, reducing fragmentation so more requests' KV caches fit simultaneously, enabling larger effective batch sizes.

drills.q: Why does kernel launch overhead matter for real workloads if it's only a few microseconds?
drills.a: A workload issuing thousands of small sequential kernel launches pays the ~3-10us fixed overhead per launch repeatedly; if per-kernel compute time is comparable to or smaller than that overhead, the overhead dominates total cost. Fix: kernel fusion to amortize launch cost and avoid redundant HBM round-trips.

drills.q: What is arithmetic intensity, and how do you use it to decide whether a kernel needs compute or memory-bandwidth optimization?
drills.a: FLOPs per byte moved from memory. Compared against the GPU's compute-to-bandwidth ridge point (roofline model): below it, the kernel is memory-bandwidth-bound and compute optimization won't help until memory traffic drops; above it, the kernel is compute-bound and reducing memory traffic won't help further.

drills.q: What do Tensor Cores add over general-purpose CUDA cores, and why does that matter for mixed-precision inference?
drills.a: Dedicated matrix-multiply-accumulate hardware (Volta, 2017+) optimized for fp16/bf16/fp8, far more efficient per cycle than composing matmul from scalar ALU instructions -- using them is what actually delivers reduced-precision throughput gains; it isn't automatic and requires the code path (e.g. autocast/AMP) to route through Tensor-Core-eligible kernels.

drills.q: Design: you're serving an LLM with a strict p99 latency SLA (200ms/token) while trying to minimize GPU cost per token. How do you reason about batch size?
drills.a: Larger batches amortize weight-loading cost, lowering cost-per-token, but every request waits for the full batch decode step, raising per-step latency. Measure actual per-step latency at increasing batch sizes on real hardware, pick the largest batch size that still clears the p99 budget with margin, and use continuous (not static) batching to adjust concurrency dynamically within that ceiling.
